question_text: Answer the following questions: A steady current flows in a metallic conductor of non-uniform cross-section. Which of these quantities is constant along the conductor: current, current density, electric field, drift speed? Is Ohm’s law universally applicable for all conducting elements? If not, give examples of elements which do not obey Ohm’s law. A low voltage supply from which one needs high currents must have very low internal resistance. Why? A high tension (HT) supply of, say, 6 kV must have a very large internal resistance. Why?

parts.part_text: Which of these quantities is constant along the conductor: current, current density, electric field, drift speed?
parts.answer_text: The current is constant along the conductor.

parts.part_text: Is Ohm’s law universally applicable for all conducting elements? If not, give examples of elements which do not obey Ohm’s law.
parts.answer_text: No, Ohm’s law is not universally applicable. An example of a non-ohmic conductor is a vacuum diode.
parts.final_answer: Thus, vacuum diodes do not obey Ohm's law.

parts.part_text: A low voltage supply from which one needs high currents must have very low internal resistance. Why?
parts.answer_text: If the voltage is low, then the internal resistance must be very low to allow high current to be drawn.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, low internal resistance is necessary for high current.

parts.part_text: A high tension (HT) supply of, say, 6 kV must have a very large internal resistance. Why?
parts.answer_text: To prevent the current from exceeding safety limits in case of a short circuit, a high tension supply must have a large internal resistance.
parts.final_answer: Thus, large internal resistance is crucial for safety.

difficulty_reasoning: Involves multiple concepts and reasoning about electrical properties.
